Hubris Comics was a pre-War entertainment company founded in 2021. It was a subsidiary of Hubris Publishing and headquartered in Washington, D.C.


== Background ==
Hubris Comics has produced various comic book series, such as Grognak the Barbarian, as well as expanding into other projects and media such as radio, television, toys and games. The Silver Shroud and Grognak the Barbarian were two of its most popular properties. The Silver Shroud franchise was particularly popular in Boston, thanks to the serialized radio drama broadcast by Galaxy News Radio. Hubris attempted to broaden its appeal with a television series shortly before the war that was instantly mired in creative differences, petty squabbles and executive interference.
In addition to print, Hubris Comics Games Studio, founded in 2062, published holotape games, such as Wastelad and Grognak & The Ruby Ruins. The Hubris Comics subsidiary also produced software, beginning with the project entitled Reign of Grelok, which was in its beta stages before the Great War.

Drumlin Diner was a chain of diners before the Great War.


== Background ==
These restaurants provided food for patrons, and were open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. They can be found throughout The Commonwealth, near Nuka-World and in Appalachia.

Fort Independence is the headquarters of the Brotherhood Outcasts in the Capital Wasteland and formerly a pre-War scientific base.  It is located west of Fairfax Ruins and north of Andale. Upon the first arrival, the Brotherhood Outcasts fortifying Fort Independence are being attacked by Raiders from Fairfax Ruins.


== Layout ==
The Outcasts have adapted the old fort to their needs and restored much of its internal facilities. All of the technology they gather is stored within in it, as are their research findings.
By default, the Outcasts inside are hostile to any trespassers. The fort is guarded on the outside by Defender Morgan, Defender Rockfowl and an automated defense Turret. After the player speaks with Defender Morgan about a job, Protector Casdin will open the perimeter fence's gate and encourage the Lone Wanderer to bring scavenged technology to them in exchange for supplies.
In the eastern section (the offices) on the main floor, there is a terminal named "Field Reports" with two audio logs that can be downloaded (Fort Independence Field Report 1 and Fort Independence Field Report 2). John Hancock is a character in Fallout 4, Fallout Shelter Online, Fallout: The Board Game and Fallout: Wasteland Warfare. 


== Background ==
John Hancock is the son of Martha and Patrick McDonough. He is the younger brother of Mayor McDonough and they grew up together in Diamond City, living in a "little shack on the waterfront". Hancock claims that during their childhood, Mayor McDonough was "entitled", "punchy" and was "the standard big brother". He also liked to shove rotten Tatoes down the back of John's shirt and slap them.According to Hancock, he and his brother had a "pretty happy childhood"
Hancock's brother ran for mayor of Diamond City with a "No Ghouls Allowed" campaign and was elected after gaining the support of people living in the Upper Stands. John confronted him in his office after his inauguration speech and begged his brother to "call it off". The mayor refused, telling Hancock that he was "carrying out the will of the people" and that he "couldn't betray the voters". No longer feeling able to stay, Hancock left Diamond City.

Elder Arthur Maxson is the last descendant of the Roger Maxson, founder of the Brotherhood of Steel. He is a character in Fallout 3, Fallout 4, Fallout Shelter Online, and Fallout: Wasteland Warfare.


== Background ==
He was born in 2267 to Lady Jessica Maxson and a high ranking paladin, Jonathan. His father was killed in battle outside the New California Republic, and his mother sent an infant Arthur east to be raised by Elder Owyn Lyons due to an unsafe environment caused by internal conflicts. 
Arthur was an attentive student that studied the Brotherhood's history. He observed a Behemoth from the Citadel walls and quoted the Codex when meeting outsiders. He was trained in combat by Sentinel Sarah Lyons, who on one occasion showed him how to kill people by stabbing them in the kidneys. He was barred from patrols due to accidentally shooting Lyons during an outing and Elder Lyons ordered Maxson be restricted from the Bailey while live fire practice was in effect. During his free time at the Citadel, he wished to befriend Liberty Prime and snuck into Paladin Vargas room to read their copy of Guns and Bullets since he wouldn't give it to him otherwise.

The Children of Atom  is a group dedicated to the worship of Atom.


== Background ==


=== Fallout 3 ===

The Children of Atom operate out of Megaton, a city built around an undetonated atomic bomb. The inhabitants of Megaton agreed not to move the bomb during its construction as they needed help from the Children of Atom to build the settlement. They are led by Confessor Cromwell and Mother Maya who still reside in Megaton. 
Members of the Children of Atom believe that the Great War was a holy event perpetrated by Atom. They believe that those who died during the war were fortunate, having been allowed to "aid in the process of Atom's creation," and hope to do the same. They refer to irradiated water as being "full of Atom's Light" and consider it a blessing and a gift from Atom.
Cromwell sent two members of the church, Tektus and Martin north of the Capital Wasteland, and Tektus refers to him as "Atom's great prophet." Another group of Children of Atom members followed Mother Curie III to establish the Apostles of the Eternal Light including the Novice and Brother Gerard.

Raiders are hostile characters in The Commonwealth in Fallout 4.


== Background ==
Raiders are described as "plentiful, ruthless, and extremely aggressive." They group together under a leader and have access to gear such as leather, combat, and metal armor. They are comprised of ghouls and humans, and use attack dogs and pipe weapons. The groups are loosely organized and follow a hierarchy.
Some gangs are more technologically advanced than others. The Forged have reactivated Saugus Ironworks and a detachment was sent to Dunwich Borers began to scavenge the pre-War quarry, subsequently shipping the products back to the Forged. A mechanically savvy gang called the Rust Devils utilize redecorated robots for their raids. What parts they cannot use to repair robots with they fashion into scrap, traps, and suits of armor. Raider leaders have managed to restore functionality to scavenged suits of power armor.

Ghouls are humans mutated by radiation and going through the process of Ghoulification, causing changes to their appearance, giving them radiation resistance, and increasing their lifespan. 


== Background ==


=== Biology ===
Ghouls are humans who have been exposed to radiation and undergo a severe mutational process known as Ghoulification. During ghoulification, the person's skin becomes dry and flaky, eventually shedding completely along with the nose, causing the individual to resemble someone suffering from severe radiation burns. The ghoulification process also extends the ghoul's life, aging much slower than a normal human, causing some to survive in the wasteland for centuries after their initial mutation. The process also renders ghouls sterile and unable to reproduce.  Further radiation exposure heals ghouls and does not impact them negatively. While most ghouls lose their hair, some retain it. Some individuals underwent the ghoulification process willingly, such as Desmond Lockheart and Eddie Winter, seeking to live forever. One woman, known as Trash, attempted to ghoulify herself at the Old Nuclear Test Site, but died of radiation poisoning instead.

Brahmin Milk is a Consumable mentioned in several Fallout games and appears in Fallout 76, introduced in the Wild Appalachia update.


== Background ==
Brahmin milk is obtained from the udder of a brahmin and is sold in establishments such as Vault City Downtown's Tap House. Brahmin milk can also be fermented, and this variant is used by Angry Rick to make his famous alcoholic "fermented brahmin milk martini" in Junction City. It can also be used medicinally. Moira Brown mentions that brahmin milk is capable of cleansing Radiation and is part of her homemade radiation remedy. 


== Gameplay ==
In Appalachia, milk can go bad over time, resulting in Spoiled Brahmin Milk. A named brahmin known as Chally the Moo-Moo produces a variant of brahmin milk called Chally's Milk, which can also spoil over time.

Radstorms, also called radiation storms, are weather phenomena that occur throughout and around The Commonwealth, Appalachia, and The Island.


== Background ==
Radstorms result in green overcast skies, audible winds, and lightning. An approaching radstorm will give off a clap of its distinctive thunder to signal its arrival. Throughout the storm, lightning periodically flashes and causes a brief spike of radiation in the area, inflicting 5 rads per lightning flash. Sheltering within the interiors of buildings during radstorms will provide protection and reduce the amount of accumulated radiation.
Radstorms directly after the Great War were often extremely violent and could result in storms capable of lifting people into the sky. These original storms would be the cause of death and ghoulification for many people who were often unprepared for such weather.
Randall Clark also describes a possible radstorm as far back as January 2078. In his description, the storm lasted two days and once it was over radiation levels had subsided from previous highs of 500. Looking outside his cave home, he found glowing green snow covering the ground.

Radiation is a gameplay mechanic throughout the Fallout Series.


== Background ==

Described as tasteless and odorless, radiation or the "phantom death" is a lingering danger present in the environment caused by the detonation of Nuclear Weapons and Toxic Waste. Measured in units known as "rads" or "sieverts," sensors outside of Vaults monitors for changes in the radiation levels as a prerequisite for entry or exit and the results of sensors placed inside are announced to inhabitants. 
Comprised of Gamma rays, living creatures that absorb too much of these ionizing rays may experience blood pooling in the gums, nausea, vomiting, anemia, diarrhea, and fatigue. Symptoms may also include loss of hair, teeth, and skin. In serious cases of radiation sickness and poisoning, living creatures will suffer from gastrointestinal bleeding, violent hemorrhaging, and death, but some life forms have adapted to the radiation in the environment.
